name: a wire edge group releases each cause whole, in order and at most once per session
topology: A sender graph with an outbound wire edge group over edges x and y (state nodes); a receiver graph with the inbound group for x and y, a fan-in F over inbound x and y, and the group's issues node. The test carries frames by hand and can hand the receiver frames it builds.
input: Open the session and deliver the first cause. Write x; write x, then y, in separate waves; write x and y in one batch; let x's node send two arrays in one wave; invalidate x and complete y. End the outbound node's lifetime and open a new one while x has no value; again after y has completed; again after x has lost its value and completed. Hand the receiver a duplicate of a released cause, an older cause, a cause two past the last, a frame with an undeclared edge, one with PENDING or RESOLVED in an array, one with an array after a terminal in the same frame, one with arrays for the ended y, and one bearing another group's name. After a cause that carried only x, subscribe a new sink to inbound y. Give the outbound group an edge value that is not bytes.
expect: The first cause carries x's and y's snapshots. Each sender wave in which an edge sent is one cause carrying only the edges that sent, with their arrays in order (two arrays stay two). Each delivery is one receiver wave: the carried edges send their arrays from their inbound nodes, the others send nothing, and F runs once; the INVALIDATE and the COMPLETE arrive as the inbound nodes' own. The new session starts the count at 1, and its first cause carries an INVALIDATE for x. After y completed, the new session's first cause repeats y's snapshot and COMPLETE: inbound y has ended, so they are skipped without an issue, and x's INVALIDATE is released. After x lost its value and completed, the first cause carries an INVALIDATE ahead of x's COMPLETE, so inbound x ends without the old value. The duplicate and the older cause are dropped; the cause two past the last is released and the gap reported; the bad frames are refused whole and their numbers taken; the arrays for the ended y, which do not end with a terminal, are skipped, the rest of their frame released and the divergence reported; the frame bearing another group's name is ignored by this group. Each drop, gap, refusal and divergence is a value of the issues node, and no inbound node ends or fails because of one. The new sink on inbound y gets y's last released value. The value that is not bytes is a throw, so an ERROR, of the outbound node. No timer is set, and nothing goes up either graph.

name: A batch delivers nothing before commit, and its topology requests follow the commit

name: A restart owner keeps one face downstream, serves each request once and makes no stale or hopeless attempt
topology: State a; a computed node u over a whose setup opens a resource; a restart owner r with its inner at r/inner over u, a sink s on r and a sink t on r/inner; rounds 2 and a retry policy of two attempts per round with a delay.
input: Let the inner complete twice, counting u's openings and closings. In a second graph let it fail once, then complete, then fail twice. Describe the topology before and after an attempt. Request a restart while the inner is live; unsubscribe s and subscribe it again; unsubscribe, request a restart while r is inactive, subscribe again, and request once more. Let the inner fail and, while its retry waits, request a restart; let the delay pass. Let the inner fail and unsubscribe s before the delay passes, then subscribe again. Let the inner fail and complete a while its retry waits. In another graph complete a while the inner is live. In another, write the restart state with 1, as a restore brings it back, subscribe s and request a restart. In another, bring r back as a restore does while a retry waited, its inner ended, one failure counted and the waiting retry recorded in its private state, and subscribe s; in one more, complete a before subscribing. In another, bring r back as a restore does with a live inner and no retry recorded, make the inner's input fail before subscribing s, and subscribe.
expect: s receives the inner's values from both rounds and one COMPLETE, after the second completion only; u opens once and closes once, when r ends, since r holds it ahead of the inner; no terminal reaches s while a restart is possible. The first ERROR is retried after the delay, the count starts again in the next round, and the second ERROR of that round ends r with that ERROR. The topology description is unchanged across attempts and t receives START at each attempt. The request on a live inner starts a fresh one without releasing a; the resubscription starts exactly one fresh inner, the old request being served already; the request made while r was inactive starts nothing beyond the fresh inner of the next activation, and the request after it starts one attempt. A retry pending when the request started another attempt is dropped and does not replace it; a retry pending when r's lifetime closed is dropped, and the new activation starts a fresh inner. When a completes while a retry waits, no inner is started over it and r ends with the inner's ERROR; when a completes while the inner is live, r ends with the inner's COMPLETE. The restored request counts as served at activation; the request after it writes 2, from the state's value, and starts a fresh inner. A retry's timer is cleared when r's lifetime closes. The owner brought back while a retry waited starts no inner at its activation: it waits that retry's delay in full, counts no further failure, and then starts one fresh inner; when a completed meanwhile it makes no attempt and ends with the inner's ERROR. The owner restored with a live inner and no recorded retry, whose inner fails at that first activation, counts that failure once and waits the delay, as an owner never captured does; it neither ends at once nor starts an inner at once.

name: The kernel adds only the settling RESOLVED, a quiet node never holds a wave, and a wave of terminals holds a fan-in
topology: State A; F over A, which sends DATA only for an even value; a quiet node Q over A, which keeps its ctx; D over [A, Q]; sinks on F, Q and D.
input: Set A to 3. Set A to 2, where Q's function sends DATA during its run. Then call Q's kept ctx.down after the wave. Set A to 5, where Q sends nothing. Invalidate A. In a second graph, give D over two dependencies B and C of one state S a manual COMPLETE policy and complete S; in a third, give D the manual INVALIDATE policy instead and invalidate S.

For 2, Q is never marked pending: D runs once in A's wave without waiting for Q, and Q's output during its run goes out after that wave as a new wave of its own, which runs D again. The later ctx.down is a new wave too. For 5, Q sends nothing and no RESOLVED is added for it. The INVALIDATE reaches Q's sink and D's at once, in A's wave, each as [PENDING, INVALIDATE]. A terminal marks the cone pending like a value: D waits for both B's and C's COMPLETE, each arriving as [PENDING, COMPLETE], and its function runs once and sees both. name: History survives a checkpoint round trip
topology: State a and a history node h over a built from its recipe, subscribed and fed a few values.
input: Capture and restore; send more values to a. Restore again, subscribe, then invalidate a and send a value. Restore again, invalidate a and then set it to another value before the first subscription; restore again and do the same with the value a had at the capture; restore again and only invalidate a. In the subscribed original, set a and invalidate it in one batch, then send a value; then set a and end it with ERROR in one batch. Restore once more and complete a before the first subscription.
expect: The history node comes back with its saved list and goes on from it. It does not run at its first activation; under the auto INVALIDATE policy the INVALIDATE after that removes its value and keeps the list, and the next value is sent with the earlier entries, as in the original. A restored node cannot see an INVALIDATE made before its first subscription; it is told only what its input holds then (R-checkpoint), so it is not always as the original, which saw it. When a was then set to another value, the restored node sends the same list as the original. When a was set to the value it had at the capture, the original has a new entry for it and the restored node, whose input is unchanged, does not run and keeps the saved list. After the INVALIDATE alone the original holds no value until the next DATA, and the restored node still holds and sends its saved list. A source that only completed before the first subscription brings its COMPLETE without its values again, so the list is not appended to. A wave in which a's value is followed by an INVALIDATE is not an entry: the node sends the INVALIDATE and no list, and the next list does not hold that value. A wave that carries a's value and its ERROR ends the node with that ERROR and no list for the wave. On every other step the original and the restored graph send the same arrays.

Reference-module tests are candidate evidence only. 2026-11-18 (graphrefly:D812): history has the auto INVALIDATE policy and keeps its list across a source INVALIDATE. 2026-11-19 (second QA; the user: "我们要be honest"): the expectation said a restored node that could not see the INVALIDATE sends the same list as one that saw it. That holds only when the value written after it differs; the two cases where it does not are now stated, both given by R-checkpoint's comparison at the first activation. Added: a wave left with no array. 2026-11-19, later: a wave with DATA and the source's ERROR. 2026-11-25 (graphrefly:D831): R-history is active; this states a current rule.

name: graphs on one thread share no wave, request queue or batch
topology: Graphs g1 and g2 on one thread. In g1, state a with sink s1, and state c with a sink; in g2, state b with sink s2.
input: Write a. During a's wave, s1 writes b and, after that write returns, captures checkpoints of g1 and of g2. During b's wave, s2 writes c. Then, in one g1 batch body, write a, then b, and read b before the body returns.
expect: The write of b is not held by g1's wave: b's wave runs at once, inside s1's callback, and s2 sees b's new value before a's wave ends. The capture of g1, which is in its wave, is refused; the capture of g2, which is idle, succeeds. The write of c waits for g1's wave to end and then runs as g1's next request. In the batch, the write of b is g2's own request: it runs at once and the read sees b's new value; only the write of a commits, when the body returns.

name: the graph layer: find, describe, observe and retain
topology: State a; computed b over a (ten times a), c over a, and d over a, whose function keeps its ctx; nothing subscribed.
input: find b and an id that does not exist; describe the graph; observe [b] and set a; observe [b] a second time, stop the first observer and set a again; stop the second. Retain c twice and release each retain. Retain d, rewire d to [a, c] through its kept ctx, and describe again and read d's definition. Have a node deliver two arrays in one invocation and stop its observer from the first callback.

After it stops it receives nothing more while the second goes on; after both stop, b is inactive. The first retain activates c, which stays active after the first release and deactivates after the second. After d's rewire, describe gives d's deps as [a, c], while d's definition still gives [a]. name: A graph that requires recipes refuses an instance without one when it is asked for
topology: Two graphs with the same nodes, one created to require a recipe on every computed instance: state a; a computed node p over a built from a recipe, with a sink; an operator o over a, built from a recipe, whose function replaces its inner node o/inner with the definition its input names; a second operator of the same shape that handles a refused replace and sends a value instead.
input: In the requiring graph: create a computed node without a recipe; replace p without a recipe; replace p with a recipe; give o a definition without a recipe and, in a fresh pair of graphs, one with a recipe. Give the handling operator a definition without a recipe. Give the other graph the same requests. Capture each graph. Restore the requiring graph's checkpoint twice, once asking for the requirement and once not, and create a computed node without a recipe in each. Then, each in a requiring graph of its own: create a computed node whose recipe names a reference no registry knows, capture the graph and restore it; create a computed node whose recipe has no reference, and capture the graph.
expect: The requiring graph refuses the node and the replace when they are asked for: no node is created, and p keeps its instance, its values and its subscribers, whose sinks receive no START. The replace with a recipe starts a new instance. o's function does not handle the refusal, so it is that function's throw: o ends with ERROR and its sink receives it; given a recipe, the inner is replaced and o goes on. The operator that handles the refusal sends its value and goes on, its inner unchanged. A state node needs no recipe. The recipe with an unknown reference is accepted, since the kernel only checks that a recipe was given, and fails only at restore; the recipe without a reference is accepted too, and its capture is refused as a missing recipe. The other graph accepts every request; its capture is refused and names the first node it holds without a recipe, while a requiring graph holds none, so a capture of it is never refused for one. The graph restored with the requirement refuses the node without a recipe as the original does; the one restored without it accepts it.

The requirement is off unless the graph was created with it, and a restored graph takes it from its host like any other graph. 2026-11-19 (QA of the D812 work): a function that handles the refusal, a recipe without a reference, a bridge group, and the requirement given again at a restore. 2026-11-19 (second QA): the two recipes no checkpoint could use are each made in a graph of their own, since either one refuses the capture or the restore the scenario then asks of the requiring graph. 2026-11-19, later (the user: "都撤掉"): the clause on a refused build of several nodes and the citation of R-bridge, both added that day, are taken out with R-node@3's sentence and R-bridge@3. Each function, at its dependency's first value, writes twice to the log and then rewires itself to add ex (X) or ey (Y). Sinks on X, Y and the log. In a fresh graph give Y's sink a callback that writes another state when Y's first value arrives. In a fresh graph let a sink of u write t during u's wave. From outside any function, in one batch body, ask Y's ctx and then X's ctx to rewire. In a fresh graph let each function open a batch of two writes to the log instead of writing twice. In the second graph let each operator's inner end, then write the source again, with B's sink subscribed first.

The rewires asked for in the batch body run in the body's order, Y's first. A batch a function opened commits as that function's request: X's commit runs before Y's. name: A function is told once that a dependency was replaced while its node stayed active, also after a capture and restore

Z over [a, b] under the manual COMPLETE policy: its function keeps in private state which inputs have completed, drops its count of an input it is told was replaced, sends what it counts and what it was told, and completes once it counts both. A sink on Z.

In a fresh graph complete sa, replace a over empty, write b, then capture, restore and subscribe to Z.

In a fresh graph with X over [a, b, a] complete a and then b; in another with X over [a, a] end a with ERROR. In a fresh graph put a computed node n between a state and X, X over [n, b, n], and replace n. name: A node's dependency list and recipe stay as they were given, whatever the host changes afterwards

name: An empty array is no output, a restart owner that can make no attempt ends with its inner's terminal, an INVALIDATE of the restart state is no request, and a pausable's locks after the wave decide for a terminal
topology: (1) A state a and a node N over [a], with a sink. (2) and (3) A state u, a restart owner O whose inner depends on u, with a sink; where a retry is needed, a policy of several attempts with a delay, and a clock the test moves. (4) A state a, a pausable P after it with its lock state, and a sink.
input: (1) N's function calls ctx.down with an empty array: alone in a run; between two arrays that carry DATA; and after the function returned. (2) The inner fails at its first attempt. In one graph end u in the wave of the failure. In two others end u while the retry waits, with COMPLETE and with an ERROR of its own, and then let the delay pass. In a fourth, with rounds left, let the inner complete as u completes. (3) Make a request; invalidate the restart state; make two requests more. Repeat with the INVALIDATE made while O is inactive, then subscribe and make a request. In another graph make one request, then in one batch invalidate the restart state and make a request. (4) Take a lock, write a twice, then in one batch release the lock and end a, with COMPLETE and with ERROR, in either order. In another graph, in one batch write a, end it and take a lock.
expect: (1) Alone, the sink receives PENDING and RESOLVED and N keeps its value; between the two arrays the sink receives those two and nothing for the empty one; after the function returned nothing reaches the sink, where a call that carries DATA starts a wave. (2) Ended in the wave of the failure, O ends at once with the inner's ERROR and starts no timer. Ended while the retry waits, O does not end in that wave: it ends when the delay has passed, with the inner's ERROR and not u's, and makes no attempt. With rounds left, O ends with the inner's COMPLETE. (3) The first request starts an attempt. The INVALIDATE starts none: the sink receives PENDING and RESOLVED and O keeps its value. Each request after it starts one attempt. Made while O is inactive, the INVALIDATE changes nothing: the next activation starts its one fresh inner, and a request after it starts one attempt. In one batch with the INVALIDATE, the request made after it starts one attempt. (4) Released in the terminal's wave, P sends the arrays it held, each as it arrived, and the terminal after them in that wave, in either order of the batch. With the lock taken in that wave P sends the terminal alone, and the value of that wave is not sent.
